correctness.rationale: Direct graph argument: deleting a single essential chord from an induced connected vertex set can leave exactly the endpoint components; its complement is one omitted interval on each of the two endpoint-to-endpoint cycle paths. This yields the exact union A_cycle ∪ {T-a-b}. Ordinary integer interval sums factor as products with both factors ≤2n and wrapping cyclic sums are complementary, so A_cycle and the long-gap sumset each have ≤2M(2n) (or 1+2M(2n)) distinct values. The short path has d-1 internal vertices, giving at most 1+d(d-1)/2 gaps. Ford’s sharp multiplication-table theorem then implies O((1+d²)n²/((log n)^δ(loglog n)^(3/2))) with an absolute implied constant, and a completing chord must have d≫(log n)^(δ/2)(loglog n)^(3/4). I independently enumerated 112 chorded labeled cycles for n=4..10 by actual induced connectivity versus two omitted paths, verifying set equality and finite bound. Checks do not prove the infinite statement; the graph decomposition and Ford theorem do.

value.rationale: It answers a motivated geometric necessity question for the same sum-completion problem: small cyclic-span repairs produce asymptotically zero coverage; any hypothetical completing single chord must be polylogarithmically nonlocal. This is a uniform structural lemma and infinite geometric obstruction, not a finite recomputation, and no existence of successful single chords is presumed.
